minutes.headline: Commission extended the grease trap report deadline to January 3rd and sharply criticised the botched software billing conversion.
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission voted to give a restaurant applicant an extension on a grease trap report, approved the October minutes, and spent most of the meeting on errors in sewer bills after the Munis software conversion. Members agreed to send a letter to the town manager and Select Board asking for better support. The Lemonster IMA wording, system maintenance, the business manager job description, and the capital plan were also discussed.

budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager tabled the commitment until the billing errors are resolved and she can talk to the town accountant.
The commission asked for an additional flow allotment over 25 years, to pay Leominster's resident rate, and for help with line maintenance and emergency services.
Rates will have to rise because of increases from Lemonster and Fitchburg; the worksheet was to be resent and discussed at the late November meeting.
Money is expected from the aqua source for sewer; further increases could change the budget and remain in flux.
The business manager wants a prioritised capital list from the CTE technician, as earlier plans centred on one generator; a rough five-year forecast was mentioned.
The owner has not paid since connection and has not supplied grease permit paperwork or invoices; the bill was described as large.
FY23 closed with more revenue than forecast due to betterment payoffs, while user charges came in under forecast, leaving a small surplus and certified retained earnings.
Of the bills sent out, a number have wrong figures; corrected bills with an explanatory letter are planned.
Members recalled the capital plan setting aside funds yearly but could not confirm the amount.
Two Sewer Commission articles transferring to other accounts are on the consent calendar.

The capital plan and maintenance program will be placed on the agenda for early January.
No meeting will be held the last week of December (December 26).
Bill will follow up with HR on the business manager job description for the Personnel Board, aiming for May town meeting.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted 5-0 on roll call to extend a restaurant applicant's grease trap report deadline to a date certain of January 3rd.
Most of the meeting went to errors in sewer bills after the Munis software conversion; some bills sent out carry wrong figures, and corrected bills with a letter are planned.
The chair will write to the Select Board and town manager asking for better support on the Munis billing problem, and the business manager will seek a personal meeting.
The business manager tabled the Q2 FY24 commitment until the billing errors are resolved and she has spoken with the town accountant.
Rates will have to rise because of increases from Leominster and Fitchburg; the worksheet is to be resent and discussed at the late November meeting.

why_it_matters: Sewer bills with wrong figures, and a quarterly commitment held back until they are fixed, touch what households and businesses on the sewer are billed and when.
Higher charges from Leominster and Fitchburg point to a sewer rate increase that residents on the system should expect to see proposed.
watch_next: The late November meeting, where the rate worksheet is to be discussed.
Early January, when the capital plan and maintenance program are to be on the agenda; the grease trap report is due January 3rd.
